title: HelioLinc3D identifies potentially hazardous asteroid 2022 SF289 from sparse ATLAS detections
summary: HelioLinc3D linked sparse ATLAS detections into PHA 2022 SF289, published by the Minor Planet Center in MPEC 2023-O26 (Jul 2023).
account: On 18 July 2023 the HelioLinc3D linking algorithm identified an unrecognized near-Earth asteroid, 2022 SF289. It was a test on archival data from the NASA-funded ATLAS survey operated by the University of Hawaii (UH). HelioLinc3D was developed by Ari Heinze and colleagues at the University of Washington's (UW) DiRAC Institute for the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. ATLAS had first imaged the object on 19 September 2022 and observed it three times across four nights. Conventional discovery requires more same-night detections. The Minor Planet Center (MPC) published the object in MPEC 2023-O26, issued 18 July 2023. It is an Apollo-type potentially hazardous asteroid about 600 feet across with an Earth MOID of 0.0015 AU and no foreseeable risk to Earth. The sources call HelioLinc3D an algorithm, not a learned model.
purpose: Built as Rubin Observatory's linking algorithm to discover moving objects, including near-Earth asteroids, from sparse multi-night detections. This benefit was that purpose.
system: HelioLinc3D (heliocentric linking algorithm for Rubin Observatory solar-system processing)
developer: University of Washington DiRAC Institute / Rubin Observatory (Ari Heinze, Siegfried Eggl, Mario Juric)
deployer: University of Washington DiRAC Institute, test run on ATLAS survey data

ratings.reason: The Rubin Observatory and UW DiRAC team obtained a real-data validation of the linking software before the ten-year survey began.
One roughly 600-foot potentially hazardous asteroid was added to the catalog. The sources state that it poses no foreseeable risk, so the benefit is knowledge, not averted harm.

ai_role.statement: HelioLinc3D linked detections from separate nights that conventional pipelines could not combine, producing the orbit that the MPC published. Caveat: UW, UH, Rubin and MPC sources call it a “next-generation algorithm”. No cited source describes it as machine learning or AI.

headline: HelioLinc3D finds asteroid 2022 SF289 in sparse ATLAS detections
metric: about 600 feet across with an Earth MOID of 0.0015 AU

comparator.against: conventional near-Earth-object discovery, which needs four observations of an object on one night
comparator.before: ATLAS had observed 2022 SF289 three times on four separate nights, but never the requisite four times on one night to be identified as a new NEO
comparator.after: It successfully combined fragments of data from all four nights and made the discovery.
comparator.quote: In retrospect, ATLAS had observed 2022 SF289 three times on four separate nights, but never the requisite four times on one night to be identified as a new NEO. But these are just the occasions where HelioLinc3D excels: It successfully combined fragments of data from all four nights and made the discovery.

later.note: On 2 April 2026 UW and Rubin announced over 11,000 new asteroids, including 33 near-Earth objects, confirmed by the Minor Planet Center and found with DiRAC-developed discovery software built by Ari Heinze and Jacob Kurlander; the release does not use the name HelioLinc3D.
later.quote: The findings were confirmed by the International Astronomical Union's Minor Planet Center (MPC), and include hundreds of distant worlds beyond Neptune as well as 33 previously unknown near-Earth objects.
